extracted.intended_audience: Florida citizens, regulated persons, agency staff, attorneys, and practitioners interacting with Florida Administrative Procedure Act (Ch. 120)
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizes statutory standards, procedural requirements, definitions, and filing/indexing duties under Florida's Administrative Procedure Act (Ch. 120), focusing on rulemaking, variances/waivers, declarations, meetings, and record maintenance. Intended as a pocket guide for persons interacting with state agencies and administrative procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variances and waivers to agency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may grant variances or waivers from rule requirements to avoid "unreasonable, unfair, and unintended results" where a person subject to a rule demonstrates the rule would "create a substantial hardship or would violate principles of fairness" (§120.542(2), F.S.). An agency must grant a variance/waiver if the person can meet the purpose of the underlying statute through other means. Agencies may not grant variances or waivers to statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner and the agency’s order granting or denying the petition must be filed with JAPC and must contain a statement of the relevant facts and reasons supporting the agency’s action. Variance/waiver decisions must conform to standards in the chapter and any uniform rules adopted pursuant to s.120.54(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to initiate rulemaking (§120.54(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person regulated by an agency or who has a substantial interest in an agency’s rule may petition the agency to adopt, amend, or repeal a rule. The agency must respond by initiating rulemaking or denying the petition in a written statement; that decision is a final action appealable under §120.68, F.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition targets an existing unadopted policy and after a public hearing the agency does not initiate rulemaking or comply, the agency must publish a statement of reasons in the Florida Administrative Register (FAR) and file it with JAPC; JAPC forwards it to legislative oversight committees, which may hold hearings and recommend legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory statements by agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency declaratory statement clarifies the agency’s interpretation of a law, rule, or order as applied to a petitioner’s individual situation. Agencies must publish each petition for a declaratory statement and its disposition in the FAR as directed in §120.565.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A declaratory statement is a final agency action and is subject to judicial review. It is an agency opinion about applicability to the petitioner’s specific circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from the APA by the Administration Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: At an agency’s request, the Governor and Cabinet (Administration Commission) may grant exemptions from APA requirements under certain circumstances (e.g., conflict with federal law or rules, inability to receive federal funds or tax benefits, compliance would defeat the purpose of the APA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may not grant an exemption until it establishes alternative procedures that achieve the agency’s purpose and are consistent with the intent of the APA. An order granting or denying an exemption, with any alternative procedures, must be provided to JAPC and published in the FAR. If granted, the exemption and alternative procedures terminate 90 days after adjournment sine die of certain legislative sessions or on the effective date of consequent legislation, whichever is earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of assistance (legislators and JAPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens concerned about agency action may contact elected state legislators or JAPC for assistance. JAPC staff may examine matters related to the committee’s statutory responsibility to review agency actions under the APA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: JAPC staff cannot represent individuals, but if an agency appears noncompliant with the Act the committee may contact the agency to seek compliance and may take other actions authorized by Chapter 120.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Agency' for Ch. 120 purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: "Agency" includes the Governor, state officers and departments, the Board of Governors, certain commissions and authorities, and other specified entities when acting pursuant to non-constitutional powers; it excludes municipalities and certain other named entities unless expressly made subject to the chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory definition lists specific inclusions and exclusions and limits coverage to entities acting pursuant to statutory powers; check the subsection for exceptions (e.g., metropolitan planning organizations, expressway authorities, entities created by interlocal agreements) to determine applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Agency action' and 'Agency head'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Agency action' means whole or part of a rule or order (or denial of petition); it includes denial of requests under s.120.54(7). 'Agency head' is the person or collegial body statutorily responsible for final agency action; agency heads serving at pleasure of appointing authority remain subject to supervision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions determine what decisions are reviewable and who is authorized to take final actions; identify whether the actor is an agency head for procedural deadlines and reviewability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirements with Division of Administrative Hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any document filed with the Division by a party represented by an attorney shall be filed electronically through the division’s website. Documents filed by a party not represented by an attorney shall, whenever possible, also be filed electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with the Division's electronic-filing rules; failure to follow e-filing requirements may affect acceptance of documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and treatment of 'Final order'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Final order' means a written final decision from specified proceedings (e.g., ss.120.56, 120.565, 120.569, 120.57, 120.573, 120.574) which is not a rule, includes materials explicitly adopted in it, is filed with the agency clerk, and the clerk shall indicate the date of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must maintain copies and indexes of final orders; final orders carry legal effect and must include adopted materials. Filing date is important for effect and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority (criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed or existing rule is an invalid exercise of delegated legislative authority if any of the following apply: (a) agency materially failed to follow applicable rulemaking procedures; (b) agency exceeded its grant of rulemaking authority; (c) rule enlarges/modifies/contravenes the law implemented; (d) rule is vague, fails to establish adequate standards, or vests unbridled discretion; (e) rule is arbitrary or capricious (unsupported by logic/facts or adopted without reason); (f) rule imposes regulatory costs that could be reduced by less costly alternatives that substantially accomplish statutory objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any one of these grounds may be asserted in challenges to a rule; the statute requires agencies to stay within enabling statutes and to follow rulemaking procedures. Use these criteria when evaluating legal vulnerability of a rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Rule' and express exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Rule' means each agency statement of general applicability that implements, interprets, or prescribes law or policy or describes procedure or practice requirements and includes any form imposing requirements or soliciting information not required by statute or existing rule. The term excludes internal management memoranda that have no application outside the agency, legal memoranda/opinions before their use in agency action, certain budget/CFO statements, collective bargaining contractual provisions, and specified Executive Office memoranda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination whether a statement constitutes a rule depends on general applicability and external effect. Exclusions are narrowly described; agencies and regulated parties should test whether a statement meets the statutory definition before treating it as non-rule or attempting challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference in rules (standards and restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule may incorporate material by reference only as the material exists on the date the rule is adopted; for the rule, subsequent changes in the material are not effective unless the rule is amended. A rule that incorporates another rule of the same agency generally incorporates subsequent amendments to the referenced rule unless contrary intent is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 2010, material may not be incorporated by reference unless: (a) material submitted electronically to the Department of State and full text is available for free public access via hyperlink from the rule in the Florida Administrative Code, or (b) posting would violate federal copyright law, in which case locations for inspection must be provided in the notice. For rules proposed after July 1, 2025, the full text must be submitted in prescribed electronic, text-searchable format and made available via an FAR hyperlink. Agencies must ensure accessibility and compliance with these technical filing requirements when incorporating external materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking is mandatory; feasibility and practicability presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking is not discretionary: each agency statement defined as a rule must be adopted by the rulemaking procedure as soon as feasible and practicable. Rulemaking is presumed feasible unless the agency proves it lacked sufficient time or that related matters are unresolved; it is presumed practicable to provide fair notice of principles/criteria unless the agency proves detail/precision is unreasonable or matters are too narrow for rulemaking outside adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies bear the burden of showing exceptions to the presumptions. Regulated persons can rely on the presumption when asserting an agency should adopt a rule rather than act through ad hoc decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and agenda requirements for public meetings, hearings, and workshops
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for emergency meetings, agencies must give notice of public meetings, hearings, and workshops by publication in the FAR and on the agency’s website not less than 7 days before the event. The notice shall include a statement of the general subject matter. An agenda must be prepared so copies can be received at least 7 days before the event; the agenda and available electronic meeting materials (excluding confidential/exempt info) must be published on the agency’s website. After publication, agenda changes are permitted only for good cause stated in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure public access to agendas and materials and document any agenda changes with stated good cause. Failure to provide required notice/agenda can implicate procedural fairness and judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency meeting procedures and burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: If immediate danger to public health, safety, or welfare requires immediate action, an agency may hold an emergency public meeting and give notice by any procedure fair under the circumstances if: (a) procedure provides at least procedural protection given by statutes/constitutions; (b) agency takes only necessary action to protect public interest; (c) agency publishes in writing the specific facts and reasons for the emergency finding and procedural fairness, contemporaneously or prior to its action. These findings are judicially reviewable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must narrowly tailor emergency actions, document factual basis and fairness rationale, and understand that courts may review those findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quorum and electronic participation for regional planning councils
rubrics_metrics.description: For regional planning councils covering three or more counties, a voting member appearing via telephone, real-time videoconferencing, or similar real-time electronic/video communication broadcast publicly at the meeting location may be counted toward quorum if at least one-third of voting members are physically present. A member must provide notice of intent to appear remotely at least 24 hours before the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must monitor physical presence thresholds and remote-participation notice rules to ensure valid quorums and avoid meeting challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and electronic transmission of agency final orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must electronically transmit a certified text-searchable copy of each agency final order rendered on or after July 1, 2015, to a centralized electronic database maintained by the Division. The database must support searching by agency name, date, type, subject, and terms in the text. Specified categories of final orders (e.g., those from ss.120.57/120.573 proceedings, certain policy-containing orders, declaratory statements, specified final orders from ss.120.56/120.574) must be transmitted. Other final orders must be listed with party names and order numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each required final order must be transmitted or added to the list within 90 days after rendering. Attach complete texts of incorporated materials, or if impractical, provide location and inspection instructions. Agencies retain responsibility for pre-2015 subject-matter indexes and may optionally transmit prior final orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of State responsibilities for indexing and electronic standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of State shall coordinate transmittal, indexing, management, preservation, and availability of agency final orders required to be transmitted. It shall provide guidelines for indexing, allow multiple indexing systems, provide storage/retrieval standards, set certification and electronic-transmittal standards to protect integrity/authenticity, determine which final orders must be indexed/transmitted, require agency reporting about precedent-setting orders, and adopt binding rules to administer these responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow Department of State guidelines and standards for electronic submissions, indexing and security. The Department may designate an alternative official compiler if the division's performance is unsatisfactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of statutory repeal on existing rules and agency obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If law provisions implemented by a rule are repealed, rules may be nullified in whole or in part depending on whether the rule only implemented the repealed provision or implemented repealed and other provisions. Agencies must publish notice of rule development identifying affected portions within 180 days after the repealing law's effective date; failure to timely publish may suspend operation of the rule portion until notice is published. If repeal causes uncertain enforceability, Department of State treats the rule per s.120.555.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should monitor statutory changes affecting their rules and timely publish required notices. Committees and the Division may notify the Department of State about rules of uncertain enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to repeal a rule that exceeds rulemaking authority (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Procedures Committee or any substantially affected person may petition an agency to repeal any rule or portion thereof because it exceeds permitted rulemaking authority. The agency must, within 30 days if headed by an individual (or 45 days if headed by a collegial body), either initiate rulemaking proceedings to repeal the rule or deny the petition in writing with reasons for the denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely agency response is statutorily required; petitioners and committees can use this mechanism to challenge rule validity under the 'exceeds authority' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on automatic expiration and retroactive rules; pre-effective adoption limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless expressly authorized by law, a rule may not include a provision making the entire rule or a provision automatically expire or be repealed on a specific date or after a period. Agencies may adopt rules prior to the effective date of the statute authorizing them, but such rules may not be effective until the statute is effective. Agencies may not adopt retroactive rules unless expressly authorized by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must ensure statutory authorization for any sunset/auto-expiration provisions and for retroactivity; adopting rules prior to statutory effective dates requires attention to when the rule may actually become operative.
